items.title: Yasin apologises, withdraws claims on drugs, money and influence in prisons
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Composer and singer Yasin Sulaiman, 51, has publicly apologised to the Prisons Department and withdrawn controversial remarks he made in a recent podcast interview. Yasin issued a video explanation on Instagram, along with a written statement expressing regret over his remarks of double standards and drug accessibility in prisons, which he said may have tarnished the reputation of the department. "I, Yasin Sulaiman, take note of the explanation given by the Prisons Department regarding several matters I shared in recent podcasts and interviews about my experiences while in prison.

items.title: NST Leader: Help workers go where the jobs are
items.summary: This allowance is not a stand-alone idea. Greater improvements have gone into the Employment Insurance Scheme, such as raising the Early Re-employment Allowance from 25 to 50 per cent of the remaining Job Search Allowance, the daily training allowance to RM30 and the maximum training fee to RM7,000. Review the RM1,000 allowance regularly rather than wait until costs rise significantly.

items.title: 5-year-old girl's prayer request becomes family's final memory
items.summary: Her grandmother, Mahani Mad Som, 63, said she found it unusual when the girl asked her father to pray with her for the first time. She asked for instant noodles with a runny-yolk egg, then asked her father to pray with her. Mahani said she realised her granddaughter was missing at about 9am after breakfast, when she found the girl's cradle empty and immediately alerted the child's father.

items.title: Erosion of Germany's political centre exposes Merz's weakening grip on power
items.summary: GERMANY'S far right and far left both made big gains in Sunday's state elections, exposing yet again the erosion of the political centre in Europe's largest economy as well as Chancellor Friedrich Merz's weakening hold on power. The AfD also recorded its best-ever result in Berlin, where the far-left Left Party came first and looks set to replace Merz's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU) in the mayor's office. Merz called the result in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania — the worst in CDU history — "a disaster."

items.title: Rauf leaves three messages for civil servants ahead of Melaka assembly dissolution
items.summary: AYER KEROH: With the dissolution of the Melaka state legislative assembly expected to be announced tomorrow, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has left three key messages to ensure continuity in the state's development efforts. "If we hold the people's trust, we must never trade it away," he said in his speech at the Melaka State Public Service Workers Appreciation Night. Also present were state legislative assembly Speaker Datuk Ibrahim Durum, state secretary Datuk Salhah Salleh and senior state executive councillor Datuk Rais Yasin.

items.title: Wira driver in viral NSE incident remanded two days
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The driver of a Proton Wira linked to a viral incident that saw a Perodua Axia crash into a ditch along the North-South Expressway has been remanded for two days. "We have also obtained a two-day remand order against the driver to facilitate further investigations," he said when contacted today. The footage shows the Proton Wira moving into the lane occupied by the Perodua Axia, prompting the Axia driver to take evasive action.

items.title: Malaysia condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has strongly condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including those targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, while reaffirming its solidarity with the Kingdom. The Foreign Ministry said Malaysia supported Saudi Arabia's efforts to safeguard its sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the safety of its population, in line with the United Nations Charter and international law. The Foreign Ministry reaffirmed the importance of Malaysia's longstanding partnership with Saudi Arabia and its commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties.

items.title: eKYC providers update systems for new-generation MyKad
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC) service providers are updating their systems to recognise the design and features of the new-generation MyKad during identity verification. The National Registration Department (NRD), in a statement, said the move followed difficulties faced by some new-generation MyKad holders when undergoing identity verification through eKYC systems. Pending completion of the updates, NRD advised users experiencing difficulties with eKYC verification using the new-generation MyKad to contact their respective institutions or service providers for information on available alternative verification methods.

items.title: MoE scraps 30pc Bumiputera equity requirement for private institutions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The education ministry has scrapped the requirement for private education institutions to maintain at least 30 per cent Bumiputera equity ownership. It said the 30 per cent Bumiputera equity threshold for institutions operating through Sdn Bhd companies, as set out in the Private Education Institution Policy Statement Book published in 2006, would no longer apply as a condition. Yesterday, the ministry said it would propose a review of tuition centre ownership rules to the cabinet next week following concerns over a proposed 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement.

items.title: E-hailing, p-hailing demand expected to surge up to 300pct during F1
items.summary: Pertubuhan Lestari Ekonomi Aktivis Digital Malaysia (Lead Malaysia) said in a statement that the projection was based on typical demand patterns seen during large-scale international events. "For delivery riders, the increased visitor numbers will also boost demand for food and parcel delivery in key areas," Lead Malaysia said. Lead Malaysia also reminded e-hailing and p-hailing drivers that as they pursue bookings, bonuses, incentives and dynamic fares, they also represent the nation.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - September 21, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Yeoh defends Loke DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke's resignation offer was the CEC's final decision and must be respected, says Datuk Hannah Yeoh. Najib fine unpaid Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar says Datuk Seri Najib Razak's family has yet to pay the RM50 million fine. Floodwaters rose quickly Ampang Jaya residents say floodwaters rose to waist level in just two minutes during yesterday's downpour.

items.title: Malaysia’s ‘elephant whisperer’ leads push to save Sabah’s endangered Bornean elephants
items.summary: This photo taken on August 24, 2026, shows Farina measuring the length of a female Bornean elephant’s leg during a GPS collaring operation as part of a collaboration involving several agencies near the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. This photo taken on August 25, 2026, shows a wild female Bornean elephant with a GPS collar around her neck crossing the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. ‘Conflict inevitable’ This photo taken on August 25, 2026, shows a herd of wild Bornean elephants crossing the Kinabatangan River in Sukau.

items.title: Trip to collect medicine ends in tragedy for 5-year-old girl
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: The 5-year-old girl who died after allegedly being thrown into a river in Kampung Padang here today had returned to Tanjung Sedili with her father to collect medication before the tragedy. Sedili assemblyman Muszaidi Makmor said the victim had returned with her 40-year-old father, who lives and runs a food business in Muar. "The suspect also returned to Tanjung Sedili with them.

items.title: Four goats killed, 20 rescued in barn fire
items.summary: BALING: Four goats were burnt to death while 20 others were saved by villagers after a livestock barn caught fire in Kampung Baru Bakai, Kuala Ketil, today. Baling Fire and Rescue Station chief Assistant Fire Superintendent Zulkhairi Mat Tanjil said the department received an emergency call regarding the barn fire at 3.35pm. "A team from the Baling station, led by Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Najmi Ismail, arrived at the scene and found the barn ablaze.

items.title: MAHB reminds road users to observe traffic rules near KKIA
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad (MAHB) has reminded road users to observe traffic regulations and practise responsible road sharing following a video showing cyclists on the access road to Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA). The video shows several cyclists riding along the airport access road, alongside other motorists. "We kindly remind and urge all road users, including motorists, motorcyclists and cyclists, to exercise vigilance, observe traffic regulations and practise responsible road sharing," it said in a statement.

items.title: Malaysia condemns Houthi attacks, stands in solidarity with Saudi Arabia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Malaysia has condemned in the strongest terms the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including those targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, and expressed solidarity with the Kingdom. Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry said Malaysia supported Saudi Arabia’s efforts to safeguard its sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as the security and safety of its population, in accordance with the United Nations Charter and international law. The Foreign Ministry said Malaysia reaffirmed the importance of its longstanding partnership with Saudi Arabia and its commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties.

items.title: Five-year-old girl found dead after uncle allegedly throws her into river in Johor
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 21 — A five-year-old girl was found dead, believed to have been thrown into a river by her uncle in Kampung Padang, Tanjung Sedili here, this morning. Kota Tinggi District Police Chief Supt Yusof Othman said police received a report at about 9:30am regarding a 37-year-old local man who went on a rampage armed with a machete while chasing a 40-year-old man. He said initial investigations found that prior to the incident, the suspect was believed to have thrown the victim into the river.

items.title: Frontken unit buys industrial land, factory buildings in Taiwan for RM118mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Frontken Corporation Bhd's subsidiary, Ares Green Technology Corporation, is acquiring industrial land and the factory buildings erected thereon in Tainan City, Taiwan, from Ginwin Technology Co Ltd for RM118.16 million. Ginwin Technology is a 53.45 per cent-owned subsidiary of Taiwan-based company, Enlight Corporation. Frontken said Ares Green currently anticipates commencing the first phase of the construction of new production lines in the first half of 2027 with an estimated investment of approximately NT$620 million (RM79.6 million).

items.title: Anwar leaves Istana Negeri Sembilan after hour-long audience with Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim held a nearly hour-long audience with Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, this evening, as a dispute over the status of the state executive council continued to unfold. Anwar left Istana Negeri Sembilan in Changkat Persekutuan here after completing the audience, Astro Awani reported. The audience came after Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council members with immediate effect late last night.

items.title: Ranhill shares jump 8pct to all-time high
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ranhill Utilities Bhd's shares hit an all time high on Monday, lifted by rising demand for industrial water infrastructure and Johor's data centre boom. In a note dated Sept 18, Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd said Ranhill is poised to benefit from the restructuring of Johor's water sector on the back of the state's tariff hike and the rise in data centre demand. HLIB said the August 2025 rise in tariff had materially strengthened Ranhill SAJ Sdn Bhd's earnings outlook.

items.title: Markets brace for tighter Fed path: CIMB Securities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Financial markets are pricing a more hawkish US Federal Reserve interest rate path than the latest forecasts from policymakers and economists: This could keep the US dollar supported into 2027, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd. The firm said markets are pricing about 80 basis points of additional Fed tightening in 2027, equivalent to roughly 3.2 rate hikes. CIMB Securities raised its end-2027 two-year US Treasury-Bund and US Treasury-JGB spread assumptions by eight basis points and 15 basis points to about 160 basis points and 270 basis points respectively.

items.title: 5-year-old girl dies after allegedly thrown into river by uncle
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Police have arrested a 37-year-old man on suspicion of throwing his 5-year-old niece into a river, causing her death, in Kampung Padang, Tanjung Sedili, today. District police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said the suspect was arrested after police received a report on the incident at about 9.30am. "Acting on information, a team from the Kuala Sedili police station went to the scene and arrested the suspect.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia stays up on bargain hunting of blue chips
items.summary: Among the heavyweight counters, Malayan Banking Bhd rose six sen to RM10.38, while Public Bank Bhd and CIMB Group Holdings Bhd both added two sen each to RM4.79 and RM7.65, respectively. Tenaga Nasional Bhd remained unchanged at RM13.04, and IHH Healthcare Bhd eased one sen to RM7.63. Jaks Resources Bhd gained 1.5 sen to 17 sen, FSBM Holdings Bhd added three sen to 9.5 sen and HHRG Bhd dipped half a sen to 16.5 sen.

items.title: Anwar conveys condolences on passing of former deputy minister Yahya Lampong
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the family of former rural development deputy minister Datuk Yahya Lampong, who passed away today. Yahya, who was also a former member of parliament for Kota Belud, died at a hospital here at 6am. In a Facebook post, Anwar expressed his sadness upon receiving news of Yahya's passing.

items.title: Govt working to expedite claims for victims of FDS helicopter crash – Dzulkefly
items.summary: TAIPING: The Health Ministry is working with the Public Service Department's Pension Division and the Finance Ministry to expedite benefits for the families of victims of the Sept 8 flying doctor service helicopter crash in Sarawak. The benefits include death ex-gratia payments, retirement benefits and other claims. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the measure was underway to ensure the victims' next of kin receive the support and benefits they are entitled to.

items.title: Ringgit ends higher against US dollar on improved market sentiment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPU: The ringgit closed higher against the United States dollar on Monday amid improved market sentiment as oil prices fell following fresh momentum for US-Iran talks. At 6pm, the local note increased to 4.0755/4.0800 versus the greenback from Friday's close of 4.0795/0840. "Market sentiment has improved somewhat, leading to the appreciation of emerging market currencies, including the ringgit," he told Bernama.

items.title: MOH moves on compensation for Sarawak helicopter crash victims’ families, flying doctor service stays grounded
items.summary: TAIPING, Sept 21 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is collaborating with the Public Service Department’s (PSD) Pension Division and the Ministry of Finance (MOF) to ensure a smooth process for granting death ex-gratia payments, retirement benefit claims, and other benefits to the families and heirs of the victims who perished in the flying doctor service (FDS) operation helicopter crash in Sarawak on September 8. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the measure is currently underway to ensure that the surviving next of kin receive appropriate justice and support. The victims who perished were medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33, medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31, two nurses, Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44, as well as pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30.

items.title: Dialog secures US$81mil Raja cluster nod from Petronas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Dialog Group Bhd has secured final investment decision (FID) approval from Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) for an US$81 million cluster development and abandonment plan. The approval covers the development and eventual abandonment of the Raja cluster small field asset under a production sharing contract (PSC). Dialog currently operates the Baram junior cluster small field assets PSC.

items.title: Powerwell bags record RM190.4mil data centre orders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Powerwell Holdings Bhd has secured two purchase orders worth a combined RM190.4 million to supply low-voltage switchgear and related equipment for a data centre project in Johor. Its wholly-owned subsidiary Powerwell International Sdn Bhd received the orders from a returning customer, with the contracts expected to contribute to the company's financial performance from the current financial year ending March 31, 2027 (FY27) through FY28. Powerwell said the combined award is the largest in its history.

items.title: 'H' series sets RTD record with RM91.2mil haul, taxi drivers to benefit – Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Special registration number H1 fetched a record RM10.78 million, leading a fiercely contested 'H' series bidding exercise that attracted more than 34,000 bidders. Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the five-day bidding exercise through the JPJeBid system, which began on Sept 16, saw 8,223 registration numbers successfully bid for out of 34,664 participants. Loke said other numbers among the highest bids were H2 at RM3.18 million, H7 (RM3.1 million), H4 (RM2,437,777) and H11 (RM1,557,777).

items.title: European Union fines Google US$462mil for data location breach
items.summary: DUBLIN: Ireland's data protection watchdog, acting on behalf of the European Union, said Monday that it had fined Google 403 million euros (US$462 million) for improperly using users' location data. The technology giant infringed the EU's General Data Protection Regulation between May 2018 and February 2020, Ireland's Data Protection Commission (DPC), which is charged with applying the bloc's rules over the issue, said in a statement. In its final decision after opening an inquiry in February 2020, the DPC ruled that Google infringed the GDPR "in respect of the lawfulness and fairness of its processing of location data in web and app activity and location history."

items.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico to sue Trump administration over White House access
items.summary: WASHINGTON: CNN, MS NOW and Politico will sue the Trump administration after being denied access to the White House, the news outlets said in a joint statement on Monday. President Donald Trump said Friday he was banning the outlets from the presidential mansion as punishment for distributing what he calls "fake news." --AFP © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar leaves Istana Hinggap after nearly an hour
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim left Istana Hinggap Negri Sembilan in Bukit Persekutuan here after an audience lasting nearly an hour with the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. Anwar sought an audience with Tuanku Muhriz amid heightened tensions surrounding the adat and constitutional crisis enveloping the state. The Negri Sembilan exco members then issued a statement on Sept 16 affirming that Tuanku Muhriz's removal in April was legitimate and Tuanku Nadzaruddin was the new ruler.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPT 21, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Bursa Malaysia's key index closed rather flat on Monday, despite increases among financial services heavyweights . In the crypto exchange, Bitcoin rose to RM343,149. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Anwar arrives at Istana Negeri Sembilan for audience with Tuanku Muhriz amid state exco shake-up
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — A convoy believed to be carrying Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived at Istana Negeri Sembilan in Changkat Persekutuan here at about 6pm today. Anwar is expected to have an audience with Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, following developments over the status of the state executive council (exco). Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim are also expected to have an audience with Tuanku Muhriz.

items.title: Najib’s residence assessed for house arrest, but location not yet finalised, authorities say
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Police and the Prisons Department held a coordination meeting today to assess the security aspects of Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s residence in preparation for the former prime minister’s house arrest. Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the meeting between the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Prisons Department took place at Najib’s residence here, however, clarified that the location for the house arrest has not yet been finalised as the authorities have not yet received the official order document. Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said police are assessing security outside Najib Razak’s residence while the Prisons Department handles detention arrangements.

items.title: Former High Court judge Duncan Sikodol joins MACC Advisory Board
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Former High Court judge Datuk Duncan Sikodol has been appointed to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) Anti-Corruption Advisory Board for the 2026-2029 term. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he presented Duncan with his instrument of appointment today. “May the trust placed in him further strengthen efforts to combat corruption while enhancing the country’s integrity and governance,” Anwar posted on Facebook.

items.title: Cops confirm arson at two 24-hour convenience stores in Kuching
items.summary: Kuching police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu said the incidents occurred between 7.05pm and 8.30pm. The fire was extinguished by Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) personnel. Alexson said police are investigating both incidents under Section 436 of the Penal Code, for mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to destroy.

items.title: Man found dead in petrol station toilet near Tronoh
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 21 — A 39-year-old local man was found dead inside the toilet of a petrol station in Taman Tronoh Baru, near Tronoh, today. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Operations Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said they received an emergency call at 2:20pm before a team of personnel from the Batu Gajah Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) arrived at the scene at 2:34pm. “Upon arrival, the police and the Ministry of Health (MOH) were already at the scene and found a man lying unconscious, as well as stuck in the toilet door frame.

items.title: ‘Urgent and important’: Serikin border complex fast-tracked for 2027 completion, says minister
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the border security project under the National Security Council (MKN) was placed in the ‘urgent and important’ category for fast-track implementation. “This project is also among the matters discussed in the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Meeting as well as the MA63 Technical Committee Council. “Do not consider projects involving national security as ordinary projects.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh: Loke’s resignation offer was DAP CEC’s final decision, must be respected
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke’s offer to resign as Transport Minister was the final decision of the party’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) and must be respected. DAP CEC deputy secretary-general Hannah Yeoh said the CEC meeting last Saturday also heard various proposals and views before the decision was made. “That was the CEC’s decision.

items.title: Beyond trade: Anwar’s fourth China visit targets AI, digital economy and skills
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou beginning Tuesday is aimed at deepening economic ties, advancing digital trade frameworks and highlighting the importance of technical talent development. “This is the prime minister’s fourth visit to China (since becoming prime minister in 2022). Anwar, who is also the finance minister, will be accompanied by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Transport Minister Anthony Loke and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.

items.title: KL mayor: Sunday flash floods hit city after Ampang, Lembah Keramat record 155mm rainfall
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — Flash floods in several parts of the federal capital yesterday were triggered by exceptionally heavy rainfall recorded in the Ampang and Lembah Keramat catchment areas. Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said the 155 millimetres (mm) of rainfall recorded yesterday was more than five times the usual 30 mm in the federal capital. “Observations showed that heavy to very heavy rain was recorded across the Klang Valley yesterday afternoon, particularly in the upstream catchment areas of Ampang, Klang Gates Dam and Lembah Keramat in Selangor.

items.title: Selangor expands Kita Selangor Voucher eligibility, households earning RM8,000 or below now qualify
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 21 — The Selangor government has expanded the eligibility threshold for the Kita Selangor Voucher (BKS) to include households with a monthly income of RM8,000 or below. It initially prioritised vulnerable groups such as single mothers and heads of hardcore-poor households before extending eligibility to households earning RM5,000 or less. “The state government has further expanded the eligibility threshold to include households earning RM8,000 or less.

items.title: JPJ nets RM91.2m from ‘H’ series plates, confirms RM10.7m winning bid for ‘H 1’
items.summary: The next highest was H 9 at RM4,969,999, followed by H 3 at RM4,209,777, H 5 at RM4,007,777 and H 8 at RM4 million. H 6 went for RM3.38 million, H 2 for RM3.18 million and H 7 for RM3.1 million. H 4 fetched RM2,437,777 and H 11 RM1,557,777.

items.title: Putrajaya condemns Al-Aqsa storming, warns provocations risk sparking wider global conflict
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — Malaysia strongly condemns the repeated incursions by the Zionist regime into the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound as an extreme provocation that violates the sanctity of al-Haram al-Sharif. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said Al-Aqsa Mosque, as the first qibla and the third holiest site for Muslims, must be defended. The statement came after about 100 Israeli settlers reportedly entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound on Sunday under tight security by Israeli security forces, ahead of the Yom Kippur observance.

items.title: 1MDB seeks Federal Court ruling, says Malaysia should hear fraud claims against UK law firm
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) has filed an application seeking leave to appeal the appellate court’s ruling that the High Court lacked the jurisdiction to hear its lawsuit against a UK law firm. She also told Bernama that the Federal Court has fixed October 12 to hear the leave to appeal application. 1MDB has put forward 24 questions of law concerning jurisdiction and consolidation of its suit in seeking leave to appeal from the Federal Court.

items.title: ‘Possibly the most effective transport minister’: Lim Guan Eng praises Loke’s RM21b infrastructure legacy in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 21 — DAP Air Putih assemblyman Lim Guan Eng said today that Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s impending departure from the federal Cabinet represents a major loss for Penang, crediting him with securing federal approval for more than RM21 billion in critical transport infrastructure for the state. In a press statement, the former Penang chief minister detailed the federal investments championed by Loke during his ministerial tenure. “With RM 21 billion of approved transportation projects in Penang, Loke is possibly the most effective transport minister who has done the most for Penang compared to the series of MCA transport ministers before him,” Lim said.

items.title: Former deputy minister Datuk Yahya Lampong dies at 86
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 21 — Former deputy rural development minister Datuk Yahya Lampong, who also served as the Kota Belud Member of Parliament, died at the age of 86 at KPJ Ampang Puteri Specialist Hospital, Kuala Lumpur, at about 6am today. The death was confirmed by his son, Masley Yahya, in a Facebook post today, although the cause of death has yet to be confirmed. Yahya served as the Kota Belud MP from 1982 to 1986 after winning the seat as an independent candidate in the 1982 General Election.

items.title: Malaysia’s air quality improves slightly, but Kapit and Serian remain shrouded in haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Air quality in Kapit, Sarawak, deteriorated steadily throughout the day, overtaking other hotspots to become the most polluted location in Malaysia as of 4pm today. Nationwide, a total of 17 monitoring stations remained in the “Unhealthy” bracket (API 101 to 200), down from the 21 affected stations reported earlier in the morning. Sarawak accounts for majority of affected areas Sarawak remained by far the hardest-hit state, accounting for 10 of the 17 unhealthy stations nationwide.

items.title: Deepavali Bazaar fees slashed 85pc, Hannah Yeoh sets RM400 cap in Brickfields
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — Participation fees for Kuala Lumpur’s 2026 Deepavali Bazaar have been cut by 85 per cent to a maximum of RM400, including the deposit, as part of efforts to reduce costs for traders. This year’s RM400 fee comprises a RM30 licence fee, RM150 service charge, RM150 site rental and RM70 deposit. In comparison, traders had to pay RM2,626 in 2025, comprising a RM21 licence fee, RM105 service charge, RM500 site rental and RM2,000 deposit.

items.title: AG: Najib’s family hasn’t paid RM50m fine, house arrest still on hold
items.summary: KAJANG, Sept 21 — Former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak has yet to pay the RM50 million fine stipulated as a condition for serving the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest. “As of now, Datuk Seri Najib’s family has not paid the fine. Najib, 73, has been serving his sentence at the Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022, following his conviction for misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Sabah electricity reserve margin rises to 19pc, expected 26pc by year‑end, says Hajiji
items.summary: “This is in line with the Sabah Energy Roadmap and Master Plan (SE-Ramp 2040) and the target of achieving a 50 per cent renewable energy capacity mix by 2035,” he said in a statement after chairing the Sabah Energy Council meeting at Menara Kinabalu here today. The Chief Minister said Sabah’s electricity supply system had shown significant improvement since the state took over regulatory control of electricity supply and renewable energy. Sabah assumed regulatory control of electricity supply and renewable energy following the approval of the Electricity Supply Enactment 2024, Sabah Renewable Energy Enactment 2024 and amendments to the Sabah Energy Commission Enactment 2023 by the State Legislative Assembly on Jan 3, 2024.

items.title: ‘Not true’, says Prisons Department as singer Yasin alleges ‘taiko’ bosses rule jail life
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 21 — The Malaysian Prisons Department has denied claims by singer-composer Yasin Sulaiman that life in prison depends on money and influence. Prisons Department senior director of prison policy Mohamad Rosidek Musa said the claim was untrue, as it has standard operating procedures (SOP) to handle misconduct or negative incidents among inmates. he told reporters after the closing ceremony of the Malaysian Prisons Department Bookathon Programme 2026 at Pengkalan Chepa Prison here today.

items.title: Ex‑farmers’ group manager faces 27 forged document charges in RM540,000 oil palm deals
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 21 — A former Area Farmers Organisation (PPK) marketing manager today claimed trial in the Sessions Court here to 27 charges of using forged documents involving oil palm purchases worth more than RM500,000. Airulnizam Island, 44, who held the position at Bernam Jaya PPK in Sabak Bernam made the plea after all 27 charges were read out before Sessions Court Judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin. The offences were allegedly committed at Bernam Jaya, Lot PT 608, Simpang 4, Bagan Nakhoda Omar, Sabak Bernam.

items.title: Did someone just win a ‘H1’ plate with a RM10.7m bid? RTD keeps everyone guessing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — A bid of RM10.7 million for the coveted H1 vehicle registration number has raised eyebrows online after bidding for the special H series closed yesterday, although the Road Transport Department (RTD) has yet to confirm the figure. Before the H series, the highest confirmed the bid was RM1.75 million for FFF 1, won by King of Malaysia Sultan Ibrahim in June 2024 and the highest amount ever paid for a Malaysian vehicle registration number. An unconfirmed screenshot shows an online bid for the ‘H1’ vehicle plate for RM10.777 million, possibly a new record for the highest JPJ number plate bid in Malaysia.

items.title: Tengku Zafrul: Asean’s next integration stage could draw on Malaysia’s NIMP 2030 principles
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Sept 21 — Asean’s next stage of economic integration could draw on the principles underpinned by Malaysia’s New Industrial Master Plan (NIMP) 2030, said Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz. Tengku Zafrul noted that Asean sits strategically between the East and West, astride some of the world’s most important trading routes. “Asean received US$226 billion (US$1=RM4.08) in foreign direct investment in 2024, almost twice the level recorded in 2015.

items.title: Socso confirms Ipoh crash victims’ families entitled to pensions and funeral aid exceeding RM275,000
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 21 — The next of kin of two victims killed in a road crash on Jalan Jelapang-Ampang here on Saturday are eligible for benefits under the Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Lindung 24 Jam Scheme for Non-Occupational Accidents. Perkeso said in a statement today that the victims were Muhammad Izdihar Rafiq Sarajil Korin and Muhamad Faiz Danial Jumri, both aged 19. According to Perkeso, the next of kin of Muhammad Izdihar are eligible for Dependants’ Benefit payments of RM945, distributed according to their respective shares, with his parents receiving the payments for life and his three siblings receiving them until they turn 21 or complete a degree.

items.title: Rauf: BN open to alliances for Melaka polls, but don’t negotiate on social media
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 21 — Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has advised parties interested in collaborating with the coalition in the upcoming state election not to negotiate such matters via social media. Ab Rauf said BN remained open to negotiations with any party concerning the Melaka state election. In the last state election, BN, led by Ab Rauf, formed the state government after winning 21 of the 28 State Legislative Assembly seats.
